headline: Trump endorses Netanyahu. He waited until nine days out.
summary: Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, nine days before Israel votes on October 27. He had held off for months as the two split over the Iran war and Gaza; in June he called Netanyahu "crazy." His post said America might not "finish the job" against Iran if Israel picks anyone else. The AP says the race is expected to be tight.

cover_question.q: Is Trump the boss of Israel?

cover_answer: No. Israel picks its own leader on October 27.
table_question: A friend says he'll only help if you pick his pal. Fair?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Israel is a country far away, and in nine days its people vote for their leader, the way grown-ups here vote. Their leader now is Benjamin Netanyahu. President Trump said on Sunday that he hopes Netanyahu wins, like a friend cheering from the stands. The people of Israel decide, not Trump.
5-7.why: A vote and a friend in the stands. Who decides is the only fact that matters here.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them a vote, which they have had in class, and a friend cheering from the stands, and it ends on who decides. The names of wars can wait. Expect "does Trump get to vote there?" No. Only people who live in Israel do.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Netanyahu wanted Trump's backing for months. They had fallen out over Iran; in June Trump called him "crazy." Sunday, nine days before the vote, Trump endorsed him with a warning: pick anyone else and America might not help with Iran. A captain who only plays if his friend is picked.
8-12.why: Fell out, waited, endorsed, warned. The captain is the mechanism.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out whether adults apply rules consistently, so the script runs the chain: a falling-out, months of silence, an endorsement nine days out, a warning attached. The captain who will only play if his friend is picked is a mechanism from their own playground. Expect "is that allowed?" Nothing stops it. Fair is theirs.

13-17.script: Endorsement or threat? Trump backed Netanyahu Sunday and said that if Israel picks "the wrong Leader," America would have to face Iran alone. Second: should a president tell another country's voters whom to pick? He did it for Hungary's Orbán, who lost, and for leaders in Japan and Poland.
13-17.why: Backing and a threat in one post. Then the rule about other votes.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Trump endorsed an ally, and he tied America's next move on Iran to how Israelis vote. The script asks which the post really is, then whether any president should weigh in on another country's vote. Expect "would you want a foreign leader telling us?" Answer straight; they check both ways.

5-7.q: Is Trump the boss of Israel?
5-7.a: No. Israel has its own leader, and its people pick him. Trump just said who he is rooting for.

8-12.q: Why did Trump wait so long?
8-12.a: They disagreed over the Iran war and Gaza.

8-12.q: Does his endorsement decide the election?
8-12.a: No. Israelis vote October 27. The AP says it's unclear what it changes.

13-17.q: Why does Trump care who runs Israel?
13-17.a: He says only Netanyahu will keep fighting Iran.
Unclear, the AP says. Many Israelis dislike his Iran ceasefire plan.
